title: French tax authority had data stolen on 680,000 taxpayers
excerpt: 680,000 rows of data stolen from the DGFiP in late June: names, addresses, and cadastral data belonging to 390,000 individuals and 285,000 businesses.
content_html:
A hacker going by the name ZeroBytes claimed on Wednesday, on a forum frequented by cybercriminals, to have stolen nearly 680,000 rows of data extracted from an internal tool belonging to the Direction générale des Finances publiques. The French treasury confirmed the breach the very next day.

The attack is not recent, however. It dates back to late June - the 26th, to be precise, according to the hacker - and the administration had detected and stopped it at the time, without ever saying a word about it publicly.

The stolen data includes names, dates of birth, addresses, and land registry information, covering around 390,000 individuals and 285,000 businesses. Passwords and bank details are not among the data mentioned.

ZeroBytes claims to have hopped from server to server before gaining VPN access - the remote entry point to the network - which then opened up several internal tax authority tools. The official account puts it more dryly, describing an identity theft that enabled illegitimate access.

A second leak is also circulating on the same forums and is said to affect around 2 million property owners, though this one has not been officially confirmed yet.

ANSSI, the government's cybersecurity fire brigade, is investigating, and the CNIL has been notified as required by law.

This isn't the tax authority's first rodeo, though. Between late January and mid-February, hackers had already fraudulently accessed 1.2 million bank accounts in the FICOBA database, using the compromised credentials of a government employee. Two breaches in one year is starting to be a lot.

For now, be wary of emails, text messages, and phone calls claiming to be from the tax authority, especially if they rattle off your real personal details to gain your trust. An exact address and correct date of birth no longer prove anything at all.

It remains to be seen when each of the 680,000 people affected will receive the little message informing them that their data is floating around in the wild.

Source: Cyberattaque.org

content_html_zh:
周三，一名名为 ZeroBytes 的黑客在网络犯罪分子经常光顾的论坛上声称，窃取了从属于公共金融总局的内部工具中提取的近 680,000 行数据。 法国财政部第二天就证实了这一违规行为。

然而，这次袭击并不是最近发生的。 它可以追溯到 6 月下旬——根据黑客的说法，准确地说是 26 日——政府当时就发现并阻止了它，但没有公开谈论此事。

被盗数据包括姓名、出生日期、地址和土地登记信息，涵盖约 390,000 名个人和 285,000 家企业。 密码和银行详细信息不在提到的数据之列。

ZeroBytes 声称在获得 VPN 访问（网络的远程入口点）之前已经从一个服务器跳转到另一个服务器，然后打开了几个内部税务机关工具。 官方账号的说法更为干巴巴，描述了一次导致非法访问的身份盗用事件。

第二次泄露也在同一个论坛上流传，据说影响了大约 200 万业主，不过这一泄露尚未得到官方证实。

政府网络安全消防队 ANSSI 正在进行调查，并已按照法律要求通知 CNIL。

不过，这并不是税务机关的第一次牛仔竞技表演。 从 1 月底到 2 月中旬，黑客已经利用一名政府雇员的泄露凭证，以欺诈方式访问了 FICOBA 数据库中的 120 万个银行账户。 一年内两次违规的情况开始变得越来越多。

目前，请警惕声称来自税务机关的电子邮件、短信和电话，尤其是当他们为了赢得您的信任而泄露您的真实个人信息时。 准确的地址和正确的出生日期已经不能证明任何事情了。

受影响的 680,000 人何时会收到一条小消息，通知他们他们的数据在野外流动，还有待观察。
